paths.description: First-visit privacy gate; captured because it blocks the public entry path.
Homepage/news feed template and primary reading discovery journey.
News archive/listing template representing dense feed browsing.
Representative article/detail reading path selected from the live homepage.

findings.summary: The homepage and poll template ignore the user’s dark preference.
findings.evidence: The CDP probe reports prefers-color-scheme: dark=true while the homepage remains light and the root computed color-scheme is normal. The archive template does switch to color-scheme: dark, showing inconsistent template support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and apply preference-driven surface/text tokens consistently across every template.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: CSS/DOM probes found no view-transition usage on home, archive, article, or poll templates, and all are multi-page navigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } with a reduced-motion fallback, then name stable shared elements selectively.

findings.summary: Long feeds provide no scroll-state feedback.
findings.evidence: The archive is 6,150 CSS px tall, but probes found no scroll-state/container-query implementation or progress affordance; the header remains static navigation chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight declarative progress/back-to-top affordance on long feeds and articles.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent gate obscures all news on first visit.
findings.evidence: The first-load screenshot shows the entire viewport replaced by consent.yahoo.com; users must choose Accept all, Reject all, or manage settings before seeing content.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep equal Accept/Reject choices but move non-essential consent into an in-page, dismissible, content-preserving surface where legally permitted.

findings.summary: Advertising dominates the first content viewport.
findings.evidence: The homepage screenshot gives most of the viewport below two navigation rows to a four-card shopping ad, and the article inserts a banner directly above and below the lead.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve smaller ad slots below the primary headline/content, cap ad density, and defer recommendation widgets until after core content.

findings.summary: Homepage and poll overflow horizontally and omit a viewport meta value.
findings.evidence: CDP measured scrollWidth 1007 at innerWidth 780 on both home and poll and visible horizontal scrollbars in screenshots; their probes report no viewport meta content. The 360px archive template reflows correctly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid viewport meta tag to every template and remove fixed/min widths from ad and page shells using intrinsic sizing and overflow containment.

findings.summary: Reusable cards rely on page-level sizing rather than container adaptation.
findings.evidence: All four template probes found no @container/container-type CSS while cards appear in main, sidebar, and narrow-feed contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and adapt card layout with size-aware @container rules, retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Many targets are undersized and desktop focus is invisible.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe counted 297 visible controls below 44px in one dimension and computed the focused sample outline as none 0px; poll counted 130 undersized controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target hit areas to at least 44px where practical and add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring that is not clipped.

findings.summary: The homepage starts an excessive request and script workload.
findings.evidence: A clean consented load issued 188 requests including 51 scripts, 56 pings, 14 stylesheets and 17 fetches; template probes observed 459 to 815 retained resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a request/script budget, prioritize only core assets, lazy-load below-fold modules, and consolidate or remove non-essential tags.

findings.summary: Third-party and duplicated page machinery dominates runtime complexity.
findings.evidence: The homepage loaded 51 scripts and 13 distinct non-Yahoo origins, while long-lived template probes retained up to 815 resources and thousands of listeners.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage/trace analysis to remove unused bundles, gate recommendation/ad code by visibility and consent, and deduplicate tag integrations.

findings.summary: Some controls and images lack accessible alternatives.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found 10 unnamed controls, 9 empty-text links and 6 images without alt; the poll found 3 unnamed controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon-only controls accessible names, ensure linked images have meaningful names, and use empty alt only for decorative images.

findings.summary: Focus treatment and heading structure are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Desktop focus computed to no outline; the homepage has duplicate H1 “Yahoo新聞”, and poll has three H1 elements including the question.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page-specific H1, preserve logical heading levels, and implement a consistent visible :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Image sizing and formats are inconsistent across templates.
findings.evidence: Home has 30 of 36 images without width+height and 30 legacy-format images; poll has all 43 images without dimensions and 30 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and responsive srcset/sizes, preferring AVIF/WebP where source quality allows.

findings.summary: The archive listing lacks a canonical URL.
findings.evidence: The archive probe found no link[rel=canonical], while home, poll, and article expose canonicals and robots.txt lists multiple sitemaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a self-referencing canonical to stable archive/listing pages and verify sitemap canonical consistency.

findings.summary: The news document has no enforced CSP and uses a permissive referrer policy.
findings.evidence: Direct target response headers include HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN, but no Content-Security-Policy or Permissions-Policy; Referrer-Policy is no-referrer-when-downgrade.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforced nonce/hash CSP with frame-ancestors, set strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter, and define a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The page exposes a broad advertising and analytics footprint.
findings.evidence: A normal home load contacted 13 non-Yahoo origins including Google Ads, Taboola, Google Tag Manager, Analytics and ScorecardResearch; 56 ping requests occurred within eight seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each vendor, remove low-value partners, batch analytics, defer non-essential third parties until consent and visibility, and document purposes.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently resolution- and format-efficient.
findings.evidence: Home reports 30 legacy-format images and no lazy-loaded images; 30 lack dimensions. Poll reports 30 legacy images. The mobile archive is better with 30 lazy images and only one legacy image.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the archive pipeline across templates: responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats, intrinsic dimensions and below-fold lazy loading.

findings.summary: Third-party resource use is disproportionate for text news pages.
findings.evidence: The text-first homepage launches 188 requests, 51 scripts, 56 pings and 13 third-party origins before meaningful interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a third-party byte/request budget, load vendors on demand, and pause/deprioritize work when content is off-screen or the tab is hidden.

findings.summary: The server-rendered 404 state provides no useful recovery content.
findings.evidence: A direct request to a nonexistent news route returns HTTP 404 with an effectively empty HTML body, offering no visible explanation, search, home link, or retry path without client execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a compact SSR 404 with a clear message, search, home/latest-news links and preserved site navigation.

findings.summary: Failure handling depends on client-side recovery.
findings.evidence: The representative nonexistent route returns an empty 404 document body, so no-JS and constrained clients receive a blank failure state.
findings.suggestedFix: Return useful server-rendered 404/5xx shells and add explicit retry/offline states for failed feed requests.

findings.summary: Memory and listener footprints are disproportionate for text pages.
findings.evidence: Post-load probes measured about 349MB JS heap on archive and 379MB on poll, 11,682 to 16,100 Nodes, and 10,789 event listeners on home.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile heap dominators and listener ownership, unload invisible ad/recommendation modules, and bound caches and feed DOM.

findings.summary: Background telemetry is chatty before interaction.
findings.evidence: The eight-second consented load recorded 56 Ping requests plus 17 Fetch and 13 XHR requests before the user performed a news task.
findings.suggestedFix: Batch telemetry, send it at lifecycle boundaries, and deprioritize or suppress non-essential background fetches.
